title: 职业球队老板：一直是男性？，吴明华拿下WNBA总冠军
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Was your birthday this week? I don't count those.
segments.zh: 这周是你生日吗？我不算这些。

segments.en: That's a bad example. The best part about being an interviewer is you get to meet a lot of interested people.
segments.zh: 这例子不好。做采访者最大的好处是能遇到很多有趣的人。

segments.en: Very often you have a chance to meet people you wouldn't otherwise get to meet.
segments.zh: 很多时候你有机会遇到平时见不到的人。

segments.en: And to see what makes them tick. I didn't really see myself as an interviewer initially.
segments.zh: 看看他们的动力是什么。我最初并没把自己当采访者。

segments.en: And very interesting to me is finding out why certain people who became leaders, became leaders.
segments.zh: 我觉得很有意思的是，探究某些人为什么能成为领导者。

segments.en: How did they rise up from nowhere to somewhere?
segments.zh: 他们如何从无名之辈崛起？

segments.en: Traditionally sports teams in the professional world have been owned by men.
segments.zh: 传统上，职业体育队一直由男性拥有。

segments.en: But now increasingly women are owning these teams as well.
segments.zh: 但现在越来越多女性也在拥有这些球队。

segments.en: One of the most influential of these owners is Clara Wu-Sai, who is a co-owner of the Brooklyn Nets and a co-owner of the New York Liberty.
segments.zh: 其中最具影响力的老板之一是吴明华，她是布鲁克林篮网和纽约自由人的共同所有人。

segments.en: And she helped the New York Liberty get to a championship than WNBA not long ago.
segments.zh: 她帮助纽约自由人不久前赢得了WNBA总冠军。

segments.en: I had a chance to sit down with Clara recently to talk about her journey from Kansas to the professional sports world.
segments.zh: 我最近有机会与吴明华坐下来，聊聊她从堪萨斯到职业体育界的旅程。

segments.en: We are in Brooklyn doing this and we're at a Brooklyn basketball center.
segments.zh: 我们在布鲁克林做这件事，现在在布鲁克林篮球中心。

segments.en: What is this center? I think it's so important what sports can teach you.
segments.zh: 这个中心是什么？我认为体育能教给你什么非常重要。
